body.statement: If \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), then \(\mathcal C_P\) is compact and convex in \(C(X_0)\), the extrema \(V_P^-\) and \(V_P^+\) are attained, and \(\Theta(P)=[(T-V_P^+)/A,(T-V_P^-)/A]\subseteq[-K,K]\).
body.justification: Attainment turns an abstract image into reportable sharp endpoints and rules out closure-only bounds.
body.gap: Finite-support shape-restriction results attain LP endpoints, but the present feasible object is a continuous function constrained by support-local cones.
body.consumer: Endpoint attainment supplies explicit least-favorable causal completions for robustness reporting and specification diagnostics.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(X_0=\operatorname{supp}_P(X)\) is closed and \(X\in I\) almost surely with \(I\) compact, \(X_0\) is compact.  Every \(u\in\mathcal C_P\) satisfies
\[
\|u\|_\infty\le M,
\qquad
|u(x)-u(x')|\le L|x-x'|
\quad(x,x'\in X_0).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal C_P\) is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous.  It is also closed in the uniform norm: if \(u_j\in\mathcal C_P\) and \(\|u_j-u\|_\infty\to0\), then for every \(x,x'\in X_0\) and \((x,z)\in H\), passage to the limit in the defining inequalities gives
\[
|u(x)|\le M,
\qquad
|u(x)-u(x')|\le L|x-x'|,
\qquad
|g(x,z)-u(x)|\le K|z|.
\]
Hence \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  Compactness can be proved directly.  Let \((u_j)_{j\ge1}\) be any sequence in \(\mathcal C_P\), and choose a countable dense subset \(D\) of the compact subset \(X_0\subset\mathbb R\).  Since \(|u_j(x)|\le M\), successive subsequence extraction and a diagonal argument produce a subsequence \((u_{j_k})_k\) that converges at every point of \(D\).  Fix \(\epsilon>0\).  If \(L>0\), choose a finite \(\epsilon/(6L)\)-net \(D_\epsilon\subset D\) for \(X_0\); if \(L=0\), take any singleton in the nonempty set \(D\).  For all sufficiently large \(k,k'\), convergence on the finite set \(D_\epsilon\) gives
\[
\max_{d\in D_\epsilon}|u_{j_k}(d)-u_{j_{k'}}(d)|<\epsilon/3.
\]
For any \(x\in X_0\), choose \(d\in D_\epsilon\) within \(\epsilon/(6L)\) when \(L>0\).  The common Lipschitz bound then gives
\[
|u_{j_k}(x)-u_{j_{k'}}(x)|
\le L|x-d|+|u_{j_k}(d)-u_{j_{k'}}(d)|+L|d-x|
<\frac{2\epsilon}{3}.
\]
When \(L=0\), every \(u_j\) is constant on \(X_0\), and the same uniform Cauchy conclusion follows from convergence at the selected point.  Thus the subsequence is uniformly Cauchy.  Its pointwise limit on \(X_0\) is uniform, and the closedness just proved places that limit in \(\mathcal C_P\).  Every sequence therefore has a uniformly convergent subsequence with limit in the class; since the uniform norm is a metric, \(\mathcal C_P\) is compact.  Each defining inequality is preserved by convex combinations, so \(\mathcal C_P\) is convex.

For every finite Borel partition \((B_j)_{j=1}^m\) of \(X_0\), the definition of \(\nu_P\), the triangle inequality, and \(|S|=1\) almost surely give
\[
\sum_{j=1}^m|\nu_P(B_j)|
=\sum_{j=1}^m\left|E_P[S\mathbf 1\{X\in B_j\}]\right|
\le E_P\left[\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf 1\{X\in B_j\}\right]
=1.
\]
Taking the supremum over finite partitions yields \(\|\nu_P\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1\).  Therefore, by the definition of \(J_P\),
\[
|J_P(u)-J_P(v)|
\le \|\nu_P\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\|u-v\|_\infty
\le \|u-v\|_\infty.
\]
Thus \(J_P\) is continuous.  On the assumed nonempty compact class it attains its minimum and maximum, which are precisely \(V_P^-\) and \(V_P^+\) by the frontier-value definition.  Since \(J_P\) is linear and \(\mathcal C_P\) is convex, \(J_P(\mathcal C_P)\) is convex; since it is also a nonempty compact subset of \(\mathbb R\),
\[
J_P(\mathcal C_P)=[V_P^-,V_P^+].
\]

In the setting of the full-law sharpness theorem, compact treatment support and the no-stayer condition imply
\[
0<A=E_P|Z|\le\operatorname{diam}(I)<\infty.
\]
The affine map \(v\mapsto(T-v)/A\) is continuous and reverses order.  The definition of \(\Theta(P)\), equivalently the already established full-law sharp characterization, therefore gives
\[
\Theta(P)
=\left[\frac{T-V_P^+}{A},\frac{T-V_P^-}{A}\right].
\]
It remains to prove the asserted deterministic bound.  For \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), \(S\) is measurable with respect to \((X,Z)\), and the definition of the conditional-mean version \(g\) gives
\[
E_P[S\Delta Y]=E_P[Sg(X,Z)].
\]
The definition of \(\nu_P\) gives \(J_P(u)=E_P[Su(X)]\).  Consequently the support-cone restriction in the definition of \(\mathcal C_P\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
|T-J_P(u)|
&=|E_P[S\{g(X,Z)-u(X)\}]|\\
&\le E_P|g(X,Z)-u(X)|\\
&\le K E_P|Z|=KA.
\end{aligned}
\]
Division by \(A>0\) proves \((T-J_P(u))/A\in[-K,K]\) for every feasible \(u\), and hence \(\Theta(P)\subseteq[-K,K]\).
